title: The Gas Trap: Outcompeting Coal vs. Renewables
abstract: We analyze a fundamental dilemma and time-inconsistency problem facing a climate coalition producing natural gas. In the short term, it is tempting to export more to outcompete coal. When this policy is anticipated, however, investments in renewables fall and emissions ultimately increase. When the coalition cannot pre-commit, its policies will be counterproductive. We discuss the robustness of this result and possible solutions. If the coalition can invest directly in renewables, for instance, the incentive to maintain a high price on exports can mitigate the temptation to reduce the price to outcompete coal. Under certain conditions, the commitment outcome can be implemented.
abstract_zh: 我们分析了一个天然气生产型气候联盟所面临的根本性两难困境和时间不一致问题。短期内，联盟很容易产生增加出口以在与煤炭的竞争中胜出的冲动。然而，当这一政策被预期到时，对可再生能源的投资会下降，最终排放反而会增加。当联盟无法做出事前承诺时，其政策将适得其反。我们讨论了这一结论的稳健性以及可能的解决方案。例如，如果联盟可以直接投资于可再生能源，那么维持较高出口价格的激励就可以缓解为了与煤炭竞争而压低价格的诱惑。在某些条件下，承诺下的结果是可以实现的。

title: Complementary Climate Policies for Supply and Demand
abstract: The traditional approach to climate policy is to regulate the demand side, for example through an emissions fee. Supply-side regulation has received less attention. The two instruments are perfect substitutes in the first best but we show that they are complements in a second-best setting with free-riding incentives. Demand-side policies alone lower the market price of fossil fuels and raise the gains from trade for a country that defects. For a treaty to be maximally robust, strong, and self-enforcing, it must properly balance supply- and demand-side instruments. The results hold with homogeneous countries and are strengthened by heterogeneity. Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.
abstract_zh: 传统的气候政策思路是对需求端进行监管，例如通过排放费。对供给端的监管则较少受到关注。在一阶最优条件下，这两类工具是完全可以相互替代的，但我们证明，在存在搭便车激励的次优环境中，二者是互补的。仅实施需求端政策会压低化石燃料的市场价格，并提高违约国家的贸易收益。要使条约做到最为稳健、有力且能够自我执行，就必须在供给端和需求端工具之间实现适当平衡。这些结论在国家同质的情况下成立，并且在存在异质性时会得到强化。NBER工作论文系列的机构订阅者，以及发展中国家的居民，可以在www.nber.org上免费下载本文。

title: Contingent Trade Agreements: Linking Free Trade and Environmental Conservation
abstract: There appears to be a tension between trade proponents and environmental activists. This paper shows, however, how Contingent Trade Agreements (CTAs) can motivate conservation. I first analyse a standard trade model where trade-specific investments (e.g., deforestation) cause environmental damage and traditional trade agreements, including free trade, increase deforestation. Next, I define and analyse CTAs, where default tariffs vary with production capacity (e.g., forest cover). In equilibrium, countries conserve to maintain favourable terms of trade. The quantitative model shows that trade liberalisation can dramatically expand Brazil’s agricultural area, but this expansion is avoidable if the EU or US offers a CTA.
abstract_zh: 贸易支持者与环保主义者之间似乎存在一种紧张关系。然而，本文表明，或有贸易协定（CTA）可以激励环境保护。我首先分析一个标准的贸易模型，在该模型中，贸易专用投资（例如毁林）会造成环境损害，而包括自由贸易在内的传统贸易协定会加剧毁林。接着，我定义并分析了CTA，其中默认关税随生产能力（例如森林覆盖率）而变化。在均衡状态下，各国为维持有利的贸易条件而进行保护。定量模型表明，贸易自由化可能会大幅扩大巴西的农业用地面积，但如果欧盟或美国提供CTA，这一扩张是可以避免的。

title: Conservation by Lending
abstract: This project analyzes how a principal can motivate an agent to conserve rather than exploit a depletable resource. This dynamic problem is relevant for tropical deforestation as well as for other environmental problems. It is shown that the smaller is the agent's discount factor (e.g., because of political instability), the more the principal benefits from debt-for-nature contracts compared to flow payments (in return for lower deforestation). The debt-for-nature contract combines a loan to the agent with repayments that are contingent on the forest cover.
abstract_zh: 本项目分析委托人如何激励代理人保护而非开采可耗竭资源。这一动态问题既与热带毁林相关，也与其他环境问题相关。研究表明，代理人的贴现因子越小（例如由于政治不稳定），相比于按流量付费（以换取较低的毁林水平），委托人从“债务换自然”合约中获得的收益就越大。“债务换自然”合约将一笔向代理人发放的贷款与依森林覆盖状况而定的还款相结合。

title: Trade and Trees
Pledge-And-Review Bargaining
Pledge-and-Review Bargaining: from Kyoto to Paris

The Conservation Multiplier
abstract: Every government that controls an exhaustible resource must decide whether to exploit it or conserve it and thereby let the subsequent government decide whether to exploit or conserve. This paper develops a positive theory of this situation and shows when a small change in parameter values has a multiplier effect on exploitation. The multiplier strengthens the influence of a lobby paying for exploitation and of a donor compensating for conservation. A successful donor pays every period for each unit; a successful lobby pays once. This asymmetry causes inefficient exploitation. A normative analysis uncovers when compensations are optimally offered to the party in power, to the general public, or to the lobby.
abstract_zh: 每个控制可耗竭资源的政府都必须决定是开采还是保护该资源，从而让后续政府去决定开采还是保护。本文提出了针对这一情形的实证理论，并展示了参数值的微小变化何时会对开采产生乘数效应。该乘数效应强化了为开采付费的游说集团以及为保护提供补偿的捐助者的影响力。成功的捐助者每期都要为每单位资源付费；成功的游说集团只需付费一次。这种不对称导致了低效的开采。规范分析揭示了补偿在何种情况下最优地提供给执政者、普通公众或游说集团。

title: Gridlock and Inefficient Policy Instruments
The Case for a Supply-Side Climate Treaty
Conservation Contracts and Political Regimes
abstract: This paper provides a flexible model of resource extraction, such as deforestation, and derives the optimal conservation contract. When property rights are "strong" and districts are in charge of extracting their own resources to get revenues, conservation in one district benefits the others since the reduced supply raises the sales price. A central authority would internalize this positive externality and thus conserve more. When property rights are instead weak and extraction is illegal or costly control, conservation in one district increases the price and thus the profit from illegally depleting the resource in the other districts. The externality from conservation is then negative, and centralization would lead to less conservation. We also derive the optimal conservation contract, and we explain when the principal, who values conservation, benefits from contracting with the districts directly even when contracting with a central authority would have led to more conservation, and vice versa.
abstract_zh: 本文提出了一个关于资源开采（如森林砍伐）的灵活模型，并推导出最优保护合约。当产权“强”且各地区负责开采本地资源以获取收入时，一个地区的保护行为会使其他地区受益，因为供给减少会抬高销售价格。中央当局会将这一正外部性内部化，从而实施更多保护。而当产权较弱、开采属于非法或控制成本高昂时，一个地区的保护会提高价格，进而提高在其他地区非法耗竭资源的利润。此时，保护的外部性为负，集中管理将导致保护水平下降。我们还推导了最优保护合约，并解释了：即使与中央当局签约会带来更多保护，重视保护的委托人在何种情况下仍会从直接与各地区签约中获益，反之亦然。

title: Improving Paris: Credibility, Technology, and Conservation

title: Private Politics and Public Regulation
Participation and Duration of Environmental Agreements
abstract: We analyze participation in international environmental agreements (IEAs) in a dynamic game where countries pollute and invest in green technologies. If complete contracts are feasible, participants eliminate the hold-up problem associated with their investments; however, most countries prefer to free-ride rather than participate. If investments are non-contractible, countries face a hold-up problem every time they negotiate; but the free-rider problem can be mitigated and significant participation is feasible. Participation becomes attractive because only large coalitions commit to long-term agreements that circumvent the hold-up problem. Under well-specified conditions even the first-best outcome is possible when the contract is incomplete. Since real-world IEAs fit in the incomplete contracting environment, our theory may help explaining the rising importance of IEAs and how they should be designed.
abstract_zh: 我们在一个动态博弈中分析国际环境协定（IEAs）的参与问题，其中各国排放污染并投资绿色技术。若可以签订完全契约，参与者便能消除与其投资相关的套牢问题；然而，多数国家更倾向于搭便车而非参与。若投资不可契约化，各国每次谈判时都会面临套牢问题；但搭便车问题可以得到缓解，显著的参与也是可行的。参与变得具有吸引力，因为只有大型联盟才会承诺长期协定，从而规避套牢问题。在明确的条件下，当契约不完备时甚至可以实现第一最优结果。由于现实中的国际环境协定符合不完全契约的环境，我们的理论或许有助于解释国际环境协定日益重要的原因，以及应当如何设计此类协定。

title: Political Treaties as Incomplete Contracts
venue: The Impact of Incomplete Contracts on Economics, Oxford University Press, 321-331

title: The Dynamics of Climate Agreements
venue: Journal of the European Economic Association 14(3): 719-752
abstract: This paper analyzes a framework in which countries over time pollute and invest in green technologies. Without a climate treaty, the countries pollute too much and invest too little, particularly if intellectual property rights are weak. Nevertheless, short-term agreements on emission levels then reduce every country's payoff, since countries invest less when they anticipate future negotiations. If intellectual property rights are weak, the agreement should be tougher and more long-term. Conversely, if the climate agreement happens to be short-term or absent, intellectual property rights should be strengthened or technological licensing subsidized.
abstract_zh: 本文分析了一个框架，其中各国随时间推移排放污染并投资绿色技术。在没有气候条约的情况下，各国排放过多而投资过少，尤其是在知识产权保护薄弱的情况下。然而，关于排放水平的短期协定会降低每个国家的收益，因为各国预期未来还将进行谈判，从而减少了投资。若知识产权保护薄弱，协定应当更为严格且更具长期性。反之，若气候协定恰好是短期的或缺失的，则应加强知识产权保护或对技术许可提供补贴。

title: The Market for Conservation and Other Hostages
abstract: A “conservation good” (such as a tropical forest) is owned by a seller who is tempted to consume (or cut), but a buyer benefits more from conservation. The seller prefers to conserve if the buyer is expected to buy, but the buyer is unwilling to pay as long as the seller conserves. This contradiction implies that the market for conservation cannot be efficient and conservation is likely to fail. A leasing market is inefficient for similar reasons and dominates the sales market if and only if the consumption value and the buyer's protection cost are large. The theory thus explains why optimal conservation often fails and why conservation abroad is leased, while domestic conservation is bought.
abstract_zh: “保护品”（如热带雨林）由一个卖方所有，卖方有动机进行消耗（或砍伐），而买方从保护中获益更多。若预期买方会购买，卖方更愿意保护；但只要卖方在保护，买方便不愿付费。这一矛盾意味着保护品市场不可能有效率，保护很可能失败。租赁市场因类似原因同样低效，并且当且仅当消费价值和买方的保护成本都很大时，租赁市场才优于销售市场。因此，该理论解释了为何最优保护常常失败，以及为何境外保护采用租赁、而境内保护则采用购买。

Games and Resources

title: Buy Coal! A Case for Supply-Side Environmental Policy
abstract: Free-riding is at the core of environmental problems. If a climate coalition reduces its emissions, world prices change and nonparticipants typically emit more; they may also extract the dirtiest type of fossil fuel and invest too little in green technology. The coalition’s second-best policy distorts trade and is not time consistent. However, suppose that the countries can trade the rights to exploit fossil-fuel deposits: As soon as the market clears, the above-mentioned problems vanish and the first-best is implemented. In short, the coalition’s best policy is to simply buy foreign deposits and conserve them.
abstract_zh: 搭便车是环境问题的核心。若一个气候联盟减少其排放，世界价格将发生变化，非参与国通常会增加排放；它们还可能开采污染最严重的化石燃料，并且对绿色技术的投资不足。该联盟的次优政策会扭曲贸易，且不具有时间一致性。然而，假设各国可以交易化石燃料矿藏的开采权：一旦市场出清，上述问题便会消失，并实现第一最优。简言之，该联盟的最优政策就是直接购买外国矿藏并将其加以保护。

title: Climate Contracts: A Game of Emissions, Investments, Negotiations, and Renegotiations
Bribes, Lobbying, and Development
Strategic Delegation and Voting Rules
Trading for the Future: Signaling in Permit Markets
How to Negotiate and Update Climate Agreements
venue: Post-Kyoto International Climate Policy, Cambridge University Press, 273-299
abstract: Executive summary Climate change is a dynamic problem with uncertain consequences. As we learn more about the benefits and costs of abatements over time, any agreement made today is bound to be renegotiated and updated in the future. Anticipating such negotiations, every country may try to influence its future bargaining power to be able to negotiate a more favorable deal. Increasing the bargaining power can be done by (i) investing less than optimally in R&D, (ii) adapting more to climate change than what is socially optimal, (iii) signaling reluctance by delay, or (iv) delegating bargaining authority to representatives that are less in favor of an agreement. Such strategic behavior makes an efficient agreement less likely. In fact, the situation with an agreement can be worse than a situation without any agreement at all. Thus, it is immensely important to determine in advance the rules governing how the countries should negotiate and update future climate change agreements. This chapter presents and discusses five such rules. First, the negotiations may be more efficient, and less strategic, if harmonization of contribution-levels is required across countries, or if the contribution-shares are pre-determined by some formula that itself is not subject to renegotiation. Second, the time horizon of an agreement should be long enough to prevent the above-mentioned strategies from being too influential. The larger the number of participants, the longer the time horizon should be. Third, the default (the outcome to which one reverts if the negotiations fail) should be the previous agreement or, even better, a very ambitious agreement. This provides an efficient starting point from which one may renegotiate the agreement.
abstract_zh: 执行摘要：气候变化是一个后果不确定的动态问题。随着我们对减排的收益与成本了解得越来越多，今天达成的任何协定都注定会在未来被重新谈判和更新。预见到这种谈判，每个国家都可能试图影响其未来的讨价还价能力，以便谈成更有利的协议。提高讨价还价能力的方式包括：(i) 在研发上的投资低于最优水平，(ii) 对气候变化的适应程度高于社会最优水平，(iii) 通过拖延来表明不情愿，或 (iv) 将谈判授权给对协定不那么支持的代表。这类战略性行为使有效率的协定更难达成。事实上，有协定的情形可能比完全没有协定时更糟。因此，提前确定各国应如何谈判和更新未来气候变化协定的规则极为重要。本章提出并讨论了五条此类规则。第一，若要求各国在缴款水平上保持一致，或缴款份额由某一公式预先确定且该公式本身不再重新谈判，谈判可能更有效率，也更少战略性。第二，协定的时间跨度应足够长，以防止上述策略产生过大影响。参与者越多，时间跨度应越长。第三，默认选项（即谈判失败时所回归的结果）应当是先前的协定，或者更好的是一个非常雄心勃勃的协定。这为重新谈判协定提供了一个有效的起点。
